# Tests that fix likeness

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`tests-fix-likeness-where-determined` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Linear tests fix likeness where both frames are determined up to likeness, and branching tests fix it where both frames are finite with decided steps and claims, by a constructive proof. Linear tests see exactly likeness with every branching postponed.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Alike configurations pass the same tests: the same courses of moves are open from each, and after each course the same claims can be realized. (`Becoming.SameTests`, `Becoming.Alike.sameTests`)
2. Where both frames are determined up to likeness, passing the same tests survives a move and is a bisimulation, so configurations are alike exactly where they pass the same tests; so too for one determined frame. (`Becoming.SameTests.after`, `Becoming.sameTests_bisimulation`, `Becoming.alike_iff_sameTests`, `Becoming.Determined.alike_iff_sameTests`)
3. Alike configurations pass the same branching tests, built from claims, failure, conjunction and that some step by a move leads to where a test holds. (`Becoming.BranchingTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.Holds`, `Becoming.SameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.Alike.holds_iff`, `Becoming.Alike.sameBranchingTests`)
4. Where the moves and claims are listed, a list holds the configurations of each frame, and whether a move takes one configuration to another and whether a configuration realizes a claim are decided, configurations are alike exactly where they pass the same branching tests. (`Becoming.FiniteDecided`, `Becoming.alike_iff_sameBranchingTests`)
5. Each step of the proof is built from the decisions: likeness to depth k is decided; where it fails, a branching test holding at one configuration and failing at the other is built; likeness to depth stops refining at a depth no greater than the number of pairs of configurations, and there it is a bisimulation. (`Becoming.AlikeTo`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.decided`, `Becoming.apart_of_not_alikeTo`, `Becoming.stops_decreasing`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.steady_within`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.steady`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.bisimulation`, `Becoming.SameBranchingTests.alikeTo`)
6. So likeness of finite decided frames is decided and is likeness to every depth and to the depth of the number of pairs; asked of every pair of frames with one configuration, one move and no claims, deciding likeness is excluded middle. (`Becoming.Alike.decided`, `Becoming.alike_iff_alikeTo`, `Becoming.alike_iff_alikeTo_pairs`, `Becoming.alike_decided_iff_em`, `Becoming.OneLoop.alike_iff`)
7. A branching test sees when a choice is made: that the first move can lead to a configuration where both of two moves can be taken holds where the choice comes after the first move, and fails where it is made at it. (`Becoming.Choosing.bothOpen`, `Becoming.Choosing.branching_apart`)
8. Neither decision can be dropped from the equivalence: that configurations passing the same branching tests are alike holds for every frame on listed configurations with one move and no claims exactly under excluded middle, and so with decided steps and one claim. In both, a configuration with three successors and one with two pass the same tests whatever a proposition is, and are alike only where it is decided. (`Becoming.alike_of_sameBranchingTests_iff_em`, `Becoming.EitherStep.sameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.EitherStep.decided_of_alike`, `Becoming.alike_of_sameBranchingTests_decided_steps_iff_em`, `Becoming.EitherClaim.sameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.EitherClaim.decided_of_alike`)
9. Where each move's outcomes are listed and the claims decided, with configurations possibly infinitely many, the same branching tests make configurations alike given this principle: of two decided families α, β, each holding at a step where it holds at the next, with α k or β k at every k, one holds at every k. For every such frame with one move and no claims, exactly under it; excluded middle gives it. (`Becoming.EitherThroughout`, `Becoming.OutcomesListed`, `Becoming.OutcomesListed.alike_iff_sameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.EitherThroughout.list`, `Becoming.alike_of_sameBranchingTests_outcomes_iff`, `Becoming.Chains.sameBranchingTests`, `Becoming.Chains.throughout_of_alike`, `Becoming.EitherThroughout.of_em`)
10. The core's branching tests are the tests of the periphery's ExplanatoryBranching, read one to one and holding at the same configurations, so passing the same tests is the same in both; on finite decided models, passing the periphery's same tests is likeness, with no classical reasoning; on image-finite models the direction from the tests to likeness is the periphery's same_iff_bisimilar, whose proof is classical. (`Becoming.BranchingTest.toTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.ofTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.toTest_ofTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.ofTest_toTest`, `Becoming.BranchingTest.holds_toTest`, `Becoming.sameBranchingTests_iff_same`, `Becoming.same_iff_alike_of_finiteDecided`, `Becoming.Alike.same`)
11. The principle of law 9 is this one: of two decided families that do not both hold somewhere, one holds nowhere. It follows from the principle that whether a decided family holds nowhere is decided, which excluded middle gives. (`Becoming.EitherNever`, `Becoming.eitherThroughout_iff_eitherNever`, `Becoming.NowhereDecided`, `Becoming.EitherNever.of_nowhereDecided`, `Becoming.EitherThroughout.of_nowhereDecided`, `Becoming.NowhereDecided.of_em`)
12. With every branching postponed until it shows, a configuration becoming the family a course may have reached, two configurations pass the same linear tests exactly where they are alike; a frame is alike to its postponement exactly where it is determined up to likeness. So linear tests miss exactly where the unfolding branches: frames branching at and after the first move are alike once postponed. (`Becoming.Frame.postponed`, `Becoming.Frame.postponed_determinedAt`, `Becoming.sameTests_iff_postponed_alike`, `Becoming.alike_postponed_iff_determined`, `Becoming.Choosing.postponed_alike`, `Becoming.Choosing.early_not_alike_postponed`)
13. Within the classes (Moore, 1956): within one frame, likeness to depth is a chain of equivalences, each finer than the one before. Where a list of N configurations holds a finite decided frame and c configurations realize pairwise different claims, the chain stops refining at some k ≤ N − c, so configurations are alike exactly where they are alike to depth N − 1; this is exact for every N ≥ 2: on a path of N places whose last steps nowhere, the first two places are alike to depth N − 2 and are not alike. Two frames read as one have configurations alike exactly where alike to depth N + N′ − 1. This sharpens the depth bounded by the number of pairs, N·N′, which is kept. For determined laws read through maps, likeness to depth k is agreement for k + 1 steps, and there one step less suffices (N − 2 within one world, N + N′ − 2 across two, each exact: Law.sameFuture_classes_exact, Identification.bounded_agree_exact); a frame's extra step is where whether a move can be taken at all shows. (`Becoming.AlikeTo.refining`, `Becoming.AlikeAcross`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.steady_within_classes`, `Becoming.alike_iff_alikeTo_classes`, `Becoming.AlikeTo.steady_within_across`, `Becoming.alike_iff_alikeTo_across`, `Becoming.EndOfPath.frame`, `Becoming.EndOfPath.classes_exact`, `Becoming.alikeTo_frameBy_iff`)
14. The tests are a bounded prefix: under a determined law read through a map, in a world a list of N configurations holds, two configurations pass the same tests exactly where their futures through the map agree for N − 1 steps (Law.sameTests_iff_within: tests fix likeness, likeness is the same future through the map, and that is agreement for N − 1 steps, Law.sameFuture_iff_within); across two such worlds of N and N′ configurations, exactly where they agree for N + N′ − 1 steps (Law.sameTests_iff_below_across, through Identification.bounded_agree). Two laws read through maps are alike exactly where their futures through the map agree at every step (Law.alike_iff_agree). No premise. (`Becoming.Law.agree_bisimulation`, `Becoming.Law.alike_iff_agree`, `Becoming.Law.sameTests_iff_within`, `Becoming.Law.sameTests_iff_below_across`)
15. Across two branching frames the depth N + N′ − 1 is exact for every pair: in a frame whose single move at each configuration is named by the map's value there and which claims nothing (Law.labelled), likeness to depth k is agreement for k steps (Law.alikeTo_labelled_iff), one step fewer than with the map's value claimed; every history with at most N states is the course of a law on N configurations (Law.realized_within, its lasso world), and such a frame is finite and decided (Law.labelled_finite). From the two courses of Identification.bounded_agree_exact, for every N and N′ there are such frames of N and N′ configurations whose configurations are alike to depth N + N′ − 2 and not alike (labelled_across_exact); read through maps, there are configurations whose futures through the map agree for N + N′ − 2 steps and which do not pass the same tests (frameBy_across_exact), so the length N + N′ − 1 of the fourteenth law is exact too. No premise. (`Becoming.Law.labelled`, `Becoming.Law.alikeTo_labelled_iff`, `Becoming.Law.labelled_finite`, `Becoming.Law.orbit_fin`, `Becoming.Law.realized_within`, `Becoming.labelled_across_exact`, `Becoming.frameBy_across_exact`)
16. Within one world N − 1 is exact for the tests: for every N ≥ 2, on the path of N places to a last one that stays, with a map taking whether the last is reached, in a world N configurations hold wholly, the first two places agree for N − 2 steps and do not pass the same tests (frameBy_within_exact). No premise. (`Becoming.frameBy_within_exact`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- alike_iff_sameTests takes both frames determined up to likeness everywhere as its condition; without it, Choosing gives a counterexample.
- A test is a finite course of moves, possibly followed by one claim; a branching test adds failure, conjunction and what some step by a move can lead to.
- alike_iff_sameBranchingTests takes the moves and claims listed and both frames FiniteDecided: a list holds every configuration, and whether a move steps and whether a claim is realized are decided.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Whether the principle of law 9 gives that whether a decided family holds nowhere is decided, or excluded middle, is not shown; showing that it does not would take a model outside the core.
- **Counterexample:** Choosing: frames choosing after and at the first move pass the same tests from their starts and are not alike (Choosing.sameTests, Choosing.not_alike), the second not determined (Choosing.early_not_determined). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Histories.lean)
- **Counterexample:** OneLoop: a configuration stepping to itself exactly where a proposition holds is alike to one that always steps exactly where the proposition holds, so deciding likeness for every such pair decides every proposition. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Likeness.lean)
- **Counterexample:** Unbounded: one configuration steps to chains of every length, another also to a chain that never ends; they pass the same branching tests and are not alike (Unbounded.sameBranchingTests, Unbounded.not_alike). Where a move has infinitely many outcomes branching tests need not fix likeness, with no principle needed to show it. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Likeness.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Reading (the AI's; Ren agreed with its direction on 14 October 2026): what linear tests cannot see is exactly where the unfolding branches (law 12); only tests that branch see it. In the periphery, branching tests fix likeness for image-finite models (same_iff_bisimilar, classically), joined to the core's bisimulation by the bridge (branching_bisimulation_iff); in the core they fix it constructively on finite decided frames, and deciding likeness for every finite frame is excluded middle. The principle of law 9 is, by its standard name, the lesser limited principle of omniscience (LLPO), here in a form for decreasing families; law 11's form, de Morgan's law for two decided existentials, is a standard equivalent; that whether a decided family holds nowhere is decided is, by its standard name, the weak limited principle of omniscience (WLPO); the Lean names stay structural, and neither is a premise. See §98 of the integration note and its section on Becoming.Likeness.

<a id="history--沿革"></a>
### History

- 2026-10-12 P76: added, following Ren's ‘move towards 100%’; see §98 of the integration note.
- 2026-10-13 takeover review: aligned the summary with the determinacy-up-to-likeness condition of alike_iff_sameTests. Without that condition tests need not fix likeness; Choosing is a counterexample, not a proof that every branching frame fails. Original theorems and witnesses are preserved.
- 2026-10-14 M4, under the plan's recommendation of short titles for the spine records, which Ren approved (“go with your recommendations”): short title, with the former title's content now the statement. Claim, proof and evidence unchanged. Former title: “Tests fix likeness where branching is determined up to likeness: where both frames are, configurations are alike exactly where they pass the same tests; without determinacy up to likeness the tests need not fix likeness”
- 14 October 2026, general laws and renames (plan section 10, study section 112): Lean sources: Unfolding only renamed (with the matching docstrings); bindings move to the new receipts (see validation scope); the study only adds section 112 (general laws and renames) and its paragraph in the English summary; chapter: §9 gains rows for Stock, LossMatching and Contacts, rewrites six rows (Capture, TimedResponse, Revision, ReferencePlan, ContinuingRevision, RepairComparison) and drops the P83 label of the Identification row; the consolidated totals follow receipt 20261013T204910.042715Z (4861 theorems, 6856 declaration audits, 86 closure modules) and the complete-episode paragraph cites that receipt; renamed Lean names in the text and glossary take their new names, and the former wording becomes “the learner given the bound” and “perturbing the state alone”. This record's claim, premises and status are unchanged; no reproof is credited.
- 14 October 2026, branching tests fix likeness (the work board's likeness row of Current math core; Becoming.Likeness): answers this record's next_delta. New laws 3–7: alike configurations pass the same branching tests; on finite decided frames configurations are alike exactly where they pass the same branching tests (alike_iff_sameBranchingTests), with a proof built from the decisions (AlikeTo, apart_of_not_alikeTo, stops_decreasing) in which likeness to depth stops refining within the number of pairs of configurations (AlikeTo.steady_within, alike_iff_alikeTo_pairs); likeness of finite decided frames is decided (Alike.decided), and deciding it for every finite frame is excluded middle (alike_decided_iff_em); Choosing.branching_apart gives the test that sees the choice. The title changed from “Tests fix likeness where determined” to “Tests that fix likeness”. Migrated to schema 2 at the same time: the claim became laws 1–2 and the counterexample; the limitation that branching tests are not stated in the core is superseded by the new laws; the readings and the absence of ethical predicates went to standard boundaries and the correspondence. Every earlier sentence is mapped in the migration table [tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.md](../../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/history/root-foundation/development/becoming-general-laws-plan/readability/migrations/tests-fix-likeness-where-determined.md); the exact earlier record is the last text_versions entry. Proof bindings for Becoming.Likeness are added after the landing run.
- 14 October 2026, the decisions, the principle needed and the bridge (the likeness row of Current math core, approved by the integrator; Becoming.Likeness and the Likeness section of Becoming.Bridge): answers both does-not-show items and the next_delta. New law 8: neither decision can be dropped from the equivalence, each exactly excluded middle (alike_of_sameBranchingTests_iff_em through EitherStep, alike_of_sameBranchingTests_decided_steps_iff_em through EitherClaim). New law 9: where only each move's outcomes are listed, passing the same tests makes configurations alike exactly under EitherThroughout (OutcomesListed.alike_iff_sameBranchingTests; the converse through Chains, alike_of_sameBranchingTests_outcomes_iff), which excluded middle gives (EitherThroughout.of_em); where a move has infinitely many outcomes branching tests need not fix likeness (the Unbounded counterexample). New law 10: the core's BranchingTest and the periphery's Test correspond one to one and hold at the same configurations (BranchingTest.holds_toTest, sameBranchingTests_iff_same), and on finite decided models the periphery's same tests are likeness, constructively (same_iff_alike_of_finiteDecided); the periphery's classical proof for image-finite models is not restated in the bridge, whose declarations must have empty axiom reports, and law 10 states that boundary. New law 11: the principle is EitherNever (eitherThroughout_iff_eitherNever), and NowhereDecided gives it (EitherThroughout.of_nowhereDecided). The does-not-show item now covers whether the principle gives NowhereDecided or excluded middle; the correspondence gives the standard names, LLPO and WLPO; the header of Becoming.Likeness was rewritten to match.
- 14 October 2026, postponement (Becoming.Postponement; Ren, 14 October: “push as far as possible, as strong as possible, generally agree with your direction”): answers the next_delta. New law 12: with every branching postponed until it shows, passing the same linear tests is likeness (sameTests_iff_postponed_alike), and a frame is alike to its postponement exactly where it is determined up to likeness (alike_postponed_iff_determined); the two Choosing frames are alike once postponed. The statement's last sentence and the reading in the correspondence say “where the unfolding branches” in place of “when a choice is made” (Ren agreed with the direction); the correspondence notes that the Lean names stay structural and neither principle is a premise; the next_delta is now a periphery model separating the two principles.
- 2026-10-15 P83e: following Ren's ‘keep prove to the deepest … for the open questions, if they need to be answered to move forward, answer them’ of 12 October 2026 06:01 and ‘offer it to them, keep proving’ of 15 October, this record's next_delta item ‘the exactness of the depth N + N′ − 1 between two branching frames’ and identification-where-bounded's ‘the instance theorem to alike_iff_sameTests’ are answered: the core module Becoming.Distinguishing is added (importing Identification and Likeness, changing no existing module), with a fourteenth law (the tests are a bounded record: N − 1 steps in one world, N + N′ − 1 across two) and a fifteenth (frames whose moves carry the registration; the depth N + N′ − 1 between two frames and the length of the tests across two worlds are exact for every pair); the corresponding does_not_show item and next_delta sentence are removed; the Distinguishing reference and proof binding are added, and the dependency on identification-where-bounded states the new reuse (re-pointed after the integrator's core checker run). See §132 of the integration note. The rest of the claim is unchanged.
